meta.title: CrewAI vs LlamaIndex: Which one to choose in 2026? (models, context & API pricing & code compared)
meta.description: Compare CrewAI and LlamaIndex architectural trade-offs, context windows, model APIs, and integration, and review side-by-side TypeScript to choose the right stack.

verdict: CrewAI fits teams building role-based multi-agent workflows where collaboration, delegation, and process control matter more than deep data plumbing. LlamaIndex fits teams building retrieval-heavy applications over private or messy data, including RAG and agentic workflows that depend on strong indexing. Many production stacks combine both, using LlamaIndex as the data layer and CrewAI as the orchestration layer. Evaluate against your workload and current release documentation.

comparison.toolA: CrewAI is built around agents, tasks, and crews: you define roles and goals, assign tasks, and let a process orchestrate collaboration. Its abstractions target multi-agent coordination and workflow control. LlamaIndex is a data framework for connecting language models to external and private data, with indexing, retrieval, and query pipelines at its center. It also supports agent workflows, but its core strength is the data layer.
comparison.toolB: LlamaIndex centers on data ingestion, indexing, retrieval, and query engines, with agents and workflows layered on top. You model documents and sources as indexes and build retrieval pipelines that feed models. Its abstractions are strongest when data access and grounding are the hard part. CrewAI centers on agents, tasks, and crews, so its abstractions are strongest when coordination is the hard part.

comparison.toolA: CrewAI provides first-class primitives for role-based agents, task assignment, sequential and hierarchical processes, and delegation among agents. This makes it a natural fit for pipelines that resemble a team with distinct responsibilities. Teams often need to verify how much autonomy and memory each agent should have in their target release. LlamaIndex offers agent and workflow capabilities, including multi-agent patterns and event-driven workflows, but its agent layer is generally used alongside its data and retrieval strengths. For orchestration-first designs, CrewAI's model tends to be more direct, while LlamaIndex's agents are often embedded in data-centric pipelines.
comparison.toolB: LlamaIndex offers agent and workflow capabilities, including multi-agent patterns and event-driven workflows that can coordinate steps and tools. These features are typically used to ground agents in indexed data, so orchestration and retrieval stay tightly coupled. CrewAI's crew and task model is more explicitly oriented toward team-like collaboration. Which is better depends on whether coordination or data grounding is the primary design constraint.

comparison.toolA: CrewAI can use tools and retrieval components to ground agents, and it integrates with external data sources and vector stores through tools and connectors. Its focus is orchestration, so retrieval depth depends on the tools and integrations you add. Teams generally need to design ingestion and indexing separately. LlamaIndex is purpose-built for retrieval-augmented generation, with extensive document loaders, index types, retrievers, and query engines. It tends to require less custom glue for complex ingestion and retrieval, especially over heterogeneous data sources. For retrieval-heavy workloads, LlamaIndex is usually the stronger starting point.
comparison.toolB: LlamaIndex provides a broad set of loaders, index structures, retrievers, and query engines designed for RAG over private and heterogeneous data. It supports many vector stores and data sources through integrations, and offers patterns for advanced retrieval. CrewAI can consume retrieval through tools, but its built-in data layer is less comprehensive. For projects where ingestion and retrieval quality dominate, LlamaIndex is the more natural foundation.

comparison.toolA: CrewAI's role, task, and crew model maps well to how teams describe work, which can shorten the path to a working multi-agent prototype. The conceptual surface is relatively focused, though production-grade memory, tool safety, and observability require deliberate design. Developers comfortable with agent-centric thinking often find it approachable. LlamaIndex has a larger conceptual surface because it spans ingestion, indexing, retrieval, and agents, which can mean a steeper initial curve for retrieval newcomers. However, its documentation and examples are organized around common RAG patterns, and teams focused on data pipelines may find its path clearer. The better experience depends on your background.
comparison.toolB: LlamaIndex exposes many abstractions for data and retrieval, which rewards teams that invest in learning its indexing and query model. For RAG-first teams, that investment often pays off in flexibility. CrewAI's smaller conceptual core can be faster to grasp for orchestration-first teams, while its production patterns still need careful design. Neither is universally easier; the fit depends on whether your team thinks in agents or in data pipelines.

comparison.toolA: CrewAI allows custom tools, custom agents, and configurable processes, and it can be extended with your own logic and integrations. Because orchestration is the core, customization often focuses on roles, task flow, and tool behavior. Teams should confirm current extension points in the release they deploy. LlamaIndex is highly extensible around data: custom loaders, retrievers, node postprocessors, and query engines let teams tailor retrieval precisely. It also supports custom tools and agent components. For data-layer customization, LlamaIndex generally offers more granular control; for orchestration customization, CrewAI is often more direct.
comparison.toolB: LlamaIndex is highly extensible around data: custom loaders, retrievers, node postprocessors, and query engines let teams tailor retrieval precisely. It also supports custom tools and agent components. CrewAI offers customization through custom tools, agents, and process configuration, with orchestration as the main axis. Both are extensible, but they extend along different dimensions, so the choice depends on where you need control.

comparison.toolA: CrewAI has grown quickly and offers features around execution and monitoring, with ecosystem integrations that continue to expand. As with any fast-moving framework, feature availability and enterprise controls can vary by plan and release, so verify against current documentation. LlamaIndex has a broad integration ecosystem across model providers, vector stores, and data sources, and it is widely used for RAG in production. Its observability story is supported through integrations and callbacks, with details depending on configuration. Both projects evolve rapidly; neither should be assumed static. For integration breadth around data, LlamaIndex often has the edge, while CrewAI focuses on agent workflow concerns.
comparison.toolB: LlamaIndex has a broad integration ecosystem across model providers, vector stores, and data sources, and it is widely used for RAG in production. Its observability story is supported through integrations and callbacks, with details depending on configuration. CrewAI continues to expand its ecosystem and production features, but its center of gravity remains orchestration. Because both frameworks change frequently, confirm current capabilities rather than relying on older comparisons.

comparison.toolA: CrewAI is a strong fit for projects that resemble a team of specialists: research-and-write pipelines, multi-step business processes, and delegated task execution. It is less compelling when the primary challenge is ingesting and retrieving from many messy sources. LlamaIndex is a strong fit for question answering over private documents, knowledge assistants, and retrieval-heavy applications. It can also support agentic workflows, but teams wanting rich team-like coordination may prefer CrewAI or a combination of both. Choosing by project shape is usually more reliable than choosing by feature count.
comparison.toolB: LlamaIndex is a strong fit for question answering over private documents, knowledge assistants, and retrieval-heavy applications. It can also support agentic workflows, but teams wanting rich team-like coordination may prefer CrewAI or a combination of both. CrewAI is a strong fit for role-based, multi-step processes where coordination is central, and less so when retrieval quality is the dominant risk. Many teams combine them, using LlamaIndex for data and CrewAI for orchestration.

comparison.toolA: CrewAI is a Python framework that you embed in your own application, so you retain control of deployment and infrastructure, though your code becomes coupled to its abstractions. The degree of portability depends on how deeply you use framework-specific features. LlamaIndex is similarly a Python framework embedded in your application, with portability depending on how much you rely on its index and query abstractions. Neither imposes a hosted platform by default, but both can create migration costs if used extensively. Planning clear boundaries around framework-specific code reduces lock-in for either choice.
comparison.toolB: LlamaIndex is embedded in your application and gives you control over deployment, with portability depending on reliance on its index and query abstractions. CrewAI is also embedded and self-managed by default, with coupling to its agent and task model. Both can be wrapped behind internal interfaces to limit migration risk. There is no inherent lock-in advantage that applies to every workload; architecture discipline matters more than the framework itself.

faq.q: Should I choose CrewAI or LlamaIndex for a RAG chatbot over internal documents?
faq.a: For a retrieval-focused chatbot over internal documents, LlamaIndex is usually the better starting point because its core abstractions target ingestion, indexing, retrieval, and querying, and it provides many loaders and retriever options. CrewAI can support retrieval through tools, but you would typically assemble more of the data pipeline yourself. If the chatbot also needs complex multi-agent coordination, consider combining them or evaluating CrewAI's current retrieval integrations against your requirements.

faq.q: When is CrewAI the better choice over LlamaIndex?
faq.a: CrewAI is the better choice when the hard part is coordinating multiple specialized agents with roles, tasks, delegation, and process control, such as research-and-report pipelines or multi-step business workflows. Its crew and task model maps directly to those designs. LlamaIndex can build agentic workflows, but if orchestration is the primary concern and retrieval is secondary, CrewAI's model is often more direct. Confirm current feature availability in your target release before committing.

faq.q: Can I use CrewAI and LlamaIndex together?
faq.a: Yes, a common architecture uses LlamaIndex as the data and retrieval layer and CrewAI as the orchestration layer, with agents calling retrieval tools built on LlamaIndex indexes. This lets you get strong ingestion and retrieval while keeping role-based coordination separate. The main costs are added complexity and the need to manage two dependency surfaces. Teams considering this should define clear interfaces between the data layer and the orchestration layer.

faq.q: Which framework is easier to learn for a small team?
faq.a: CrewAI's conceptual core around agents, tasks, and crews is relatively compact and can be quick to grasp for orchestration-first teams, while LlamaIndex spans ingestion, indexing, retrieval, and agents, which is broader but well organized around RAG patterns. Neither is universally easier; the fit depends on whether your team thinks in agent workflows or data pipelines. For a small team building retrieval-heavy features, LlamaIndex's examples may shorten the path, whereas orchestration-heavy teams may prefer CrewAI.

faq.q: Are there security or compliance differences between CrewAI and LlamaIndex?
faq.a: Both are frameworks that you typically embed in your own application, so security and compliance depend heavily on your deployment, data handling, model providers, and configuration rather than on the framework alone. You should review current documentation and any enterprise offerings for features such as access controls, audit logging, and data residency, which can vary by version and plan. Do not assume parity across releases; verify the specific controls your organization requires.

faq.q: Which option scales better for production workloads?
faq.a: Scalability depends more on architecture and workload than on the framework brand: retrieval latency, model throughput, concurrency, and external service limits often dominate. LlamaIndex provides many options for vector stores and retrieval patterns that can be tuned, while CrewAI's orchestration can introduce multiple model calls per task, which affects cost and latency. Load test your actual design and review current guidance for both frameworks rather than relying on generic claims.

faq.q: Do CrewAI or LlamaIndex lock me into a vendor?
faq.a: Neither framework inherently requires a specific hosted platform, since both are typically embedded in your own Python application, but your code becomes coupled to their abstractions as you adopt them more deeply. Migration cost depends on how many framework-specific features you use and how well you isolate them behind internal interfaces. Planning clear boundaries and avoiding unnecessary coupling reduces lock-in risk with either choice.

faq.q: What is a practical way to evaluate both for my 2026 project?
faq.a: Build a small proof of concept around your riskiest requirement: if retrieval quality over messy data is the risk, test LlamaIndex indexing and retrieval; if multi-agent coordination is the risk, test CrewAI crews and task flow. Measure outcomes such as answer quality, latency, cost per task, and developer time, using your own data and configuration. Because both frameworks evolve quickly, base the decision on current releases and documentation rather than older comparisons.
